title: Follow Up Request for Information for FDA Scientific Instrument Repair and Maintenance Recompete
agency: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF > FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION > FDA OFFICE OF ACQ  GRANT SVCS
description:
Purpose and requested industry input  

 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requests completion of the attached Excel questionnaire to help the Government determine the best acquisition strategy and pricing structure for its scientific instrument repair and maintenance recompete. FDA seeks the most cost-effective approach with the least administrative burden while preserving responsive, qualified service. 

 FDA intends to establish an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with firm-fixed-price (FFP) amounts or rates where practicable. Industry input will inform service delivery arrangements, whether service plans can be prepriced at IDIQ award and on what basis, service-manager handling charges, program management pricing, and platform capabilities. Written alternatives should explain their pricing basis, limitations, and expected benefit. 

  Scope  

 The anticipated scope includes managing, coordinating, and performing repair and maintenance of scientific instruments, integrated systems, and equipment supporting FDA laboratory operations at locations identified in task orders. Services include coverage administration, request intake and routing, quotations, preventive maintenance (PM) scheduling and tracking, diagnostics, repairs, parts, calibration when ordered, service records, reporting, and invoice reconciliation at the IDIQ and task-order levels. 

 Representative equipment includes mass spectrometers; liquid and gas chromatographs; infrared, Raman, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometers; electron and optical microscopes; surface analysis instruments; DNA sequencers, analyzers, and extraction systems; microbial identification systems; flow cytometers; centrifuges; incubators and shakers; autoclaves; vacuum pumps; and laboratory refrigeration and freezers. Integrated systems may include multiple manufacturers’ components, control computers, and software. These examples do not establish model-specific serviceability. 

 For planning purposes, approximately 1,000 instruments are anticipated across FDA Centers in the United States and Puerto Rico. The preliminary site count includes approximately 25 laboratories within 17 cities: Dauphin Island, Alabama; Jefferson, Arkansas; Alameda and Irvine, California; Lakewood, Colorado; Atlanta, Georgia; Bedford Park, Illinois; Lenexa, Kansas; College Park, Laurel, and Silver Spring, Maryland; Winchester, Massachusetts; Detroit, Michigan; Jamaica, New York; Cincinnati, Ohio; Bothell, Washington; and San Juan, Puerto Rico. The questionnaire provides historical activity for informational and planning purposes only. These data have not been independently validated and do not constitute guaranteed demand or a verified count of future payable transactions. 

  Coverage and pricing definitions  

  Comprehensive plan and action.  A purchased plan covers the technical services expressly identified for its coverage period, which may include PM, diagnostics, repairs, labor, parts, travel, and support, subject to stated exclusions. A comprehensive action is an authorized service request within that purchased coverage; included technical work is not separately charged again. 

  As-needed action.  An authorized request for technical service outside existing purchased coverage, including equipment without a plan or an excluded service. The provider price and required Government authorization are established before the work. As-needed describes demand and does not require time-and-materials pricing. Work included in repair-only or standalone PM plans remains covered work. 

  Administration and service delivery definitions  

  Service manager and service provider.  The service manager administers coverage and coordinates requests. The service provider performs technical maintenance, repair, or calibration. Identify direct and subcontracted work. 

  Provider price, handling charge, and PMO.  The provider price pays for authorized technical work and included costs. A handling charge compensates request-level administration. Program management office (PMO) pricing addresses overall IDIQ and task-order administration, including scheduling, invoicing, PM tracking and management, and reporting. Industry should identify which activities each price includes. Work paid through one element must not be charged again through another; multiple quotes, visits, or invoices for the same request must not create duplicate handling charges. 

  In-house and subcontracted repairs.  In-house means work performed by the respondent’s own employees at FDA sites or its facilities. Subcontracted work is performed by another organization, including an original equipment manufacturer (OEM), authorized provider, or independent service firm. Identify applicable testing/calibration accreditation and scope separately from repair capability. 

  Service priority and timing definitions  

  Priority.  Failure threatens time-sensitive work, research results, or sample integrity. The proposed on-site response target is within three business days; urgent support or faster response may be necessary. 

  Standard.  Failure affects operations, but a temporary workaround or alternate instrument permits work to continue. The proposed on-site response target is within seven business days. This corresponds to the questionnaire’s routine-response category. 

  Non-time-critical.  Service can be deferred without materially affecting current laboratory work, results, or samples. The proposed on-site response target is within twenty business days. This corresponds to the questionnaire’s non-critical category. 

 FDA assigns priority based on operational impact. Acknowledgment confirms receipt; the proposed target is one business day. On-site response means technician arrival ready to work. Restoration means return to the required operating condition and is separate from arrival. One business day is not equivalent to 24 calendar hours. Industr
